extracted.intended_audience: general readers, film fans, researchers or students of film and film criticism
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the 2007 Judd Apatow film Knocked Up, its plot, production, reception, controversies, box-office performance, and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box office performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of commercial success such as opening weekend rank and gross (the film opened at No. 2 with $30,690,990 in its opening weekend; domestically $148,768,917; foreign $70,307,601; totaling $219,076,518). The film also 'spent eight weeks in the box office top ten.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an indicator of unexpected financial success; the article also notes industry analysis attributing success to the use of radio and television ads in combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical response — aggregator scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregated critic/audience metrics cited as measures of critical reception: 'On Rotten Tomatoes, Knocked Up has an approval rating of 90% ... average rating of 7.7/10.' 'On Metacritic, the film has a score of 85 out of 100.' 'Audiences surveyed by CinemaScore gave the film an average grade of "B+".'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article includes the Rotten Tomatoes critical consensus quote: 'Knocked Up is a hilarious, poignant and refreshing look at the rigors of courtship and child-rearing, with a sometimes raunchy, yet savvy script that is ably acted and directed.' These aggregator scores are treated as summary indicators of critical and audience reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor and comedic effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics' assessments of how funny the film is are a central evaluative dimension: reviewers call it 'hilarious,' 'explosively funny,' and note that 'the laughs are plentiful.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even reviews that note flaws often praise the film's comic moments (e.g., 'the loony, incidental throwaway moments that really make an impression'), indicating that the strength of comedic material can outweigh other weaknesses in evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative cohesion and editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical commentary about story structure and pacing: reviewers said 'the central story doesn't quite gel,' 'the storyline meanders and too many scenes drone on,' and that the film 'is in serious need of a good editor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative coherence and tight editing are presented as criteria that can diminish overall assessment even when comedic elements are strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of gender / accusations of sexism
rubrics_metrics.description: Debate over whether the film propagates sexist attitudes: early reviews and commentators claimed the film 'paint(s) the women as shrews, as humorless and uptight, and it paints the men as lovable, goofy, fun-loving guys.' Katherine Heigl described the film as 'a little sexist.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is treated as a substantive critical dimension: multiple critics, a public debate, and responses from the director (acknowledging characters 'are sexist at times' and positioning them as immature) are recorded—making gender portrayal a criterion for evaluating the film's cultural and ethical value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural impact / discussion value
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the film's role in broader cultural conversations: Time magazine suggested the film's 'unexpected short-term success' may be attributable to a sociological phenomenon—'shock value, sexual humor, and historically taboo themes' that created a nationwide discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural impact and the ability to provoke discussion are presented as alternative explanations for commercial/critical attention and as criteria in judging the film's significance beyond artistic merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards, honors and critics' top-ten lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition by institutions and critics as measures of esteem: inclusion on the American Film Institute's ten best movies of the year, placement on many critics' top-ten lists, nominations (e.g., Writers Guild of America Award for Best Original Screenplay), and wins such as Teen Choice Award 'Choice: Comedy' and a High Times Stony Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards and year-end lists are presented as formal markers of achievement and critical approval that supplement box-office and aggregator metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / allegations of copyright infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims regarding the film's originality, specifically allegations that it bore similarities to Rebecca Eckler's book 'Knocked Up: Confessions of a Hip Mother-to-Be' and a subsequent lawsuit for copyright infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations of substantial similarity and legal action are recorded as factors that may affect evaluations of originality and ethical/professional standing; the director's public statement that the works are 'two very different stories about a common experience' is also noted.
